subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated inference reservoir — proposal & decision grid
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@custodycare.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated inference reservoir — proposal & decision grid

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain points you called out:
- Unpredictable inference latency at peak business hours; intermittent p95 spikes > 800ms impacting UX.
- Multi-tenant noisy-neighbor concerns for models that process PHI — need stronger isolation guarantees.
- Nightly batch scoring (off-peak) that must finish within a tight 2–3 hour window.
- Cost sensitivity: team wants to avoid large upfront hardware ops but needs predictability for budgeting.

Stated goals / success metrics:
- p95 latency target for production traffic: < 400ms (soft) / < 350ms (stretch) for 13B tuned model.
- Throughput: steady-state ~1.2–1.8M tokens/day; nightly batch peak ~6–8M tokens over 2–3 hours.
- Isolation: single-tenant reserved pool for PHI workloads + auditability (KMS, audit logs).
- SLA ask: 99.95% uptime for the reserved pool and a latency SLO for p95 within defined load profile.

What we propose next (attached decision grid + proposal):
- Decision grid (attached) with two recommended configurations: Dedicated-reserved pool (single-tenant) vs Hybrid-reserved + burst. Each row maps expected latency, unit cost, and procurement commitment.
- Technical workshop to validate load profile and confirm burst windows (30–60m) for nightly batch.
- Procurement checklist: SOC 2 Type II, data residency in US-West, and standard DPA language.

Attachments included: custodycare_decision_grid_v1.xlsx, capacity_proposal_v3.pdf, isolation_topology.png (diagram).

Immediate asks from CustodyCare: please confirm preferred configuration (Option A or B in the grid) and target procurement date so we can size the reserved pool and draft a Mutual Action Plan.

If it helps, we can run a short 72-hour canary on a small dedicated slice to validate latency before a full commit.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

---
Attachment: custodycare_decision_grid_v1.xlsx (Excel, 6 rows)
Attachment: capacity_proposal_v3.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)
Attachment: isolation_topology.png (PNG, 1 image)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@custodycare.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@custodycare.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated inference reservoir — proposal & decision grid

Priya — thanks for the fast recap and the doc set. Helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Can you produce two formal price points for the configurations in the grid? We’d like: (a) small dedicated pool with strict isolation (minimal burst) and (b) medium reserved + burst into shared for cost amortization. Include monthly committed spend and overage rates.
2) Procurement asked for current SOC 2 Type II report and an export of data residency options (we need US-West/central).
3) How do you handle model fallbacks for latency SLOs? If we hit a p95 degradation, can Redwood automatically fallback to a smaller quantized variant for a percentage of traffic?

Our internal timeline is: procurement review week of Jul 19, exec budget sign-off by Aug 2. If we can get pricing + SOC2 by Mon 13 Jul, we’ll slot a technical validation session the following week.

Alex Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | CustodyCare
alex.turner@custodycare.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@custodycare.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated inference reservoir — proposal & decision grid

Alex — great, thanks. Short answers and next steps below. Full line-item pricing and SOC 2 PDF attached (capacity_proposal_v3.pdf includes the numbers).

1) Pricing options (summary):
   - Option A (Strict Dedicated): 4x reserved GPUs (single-tenant pool), monthly commit; designed for p95 < 350ms at your stated load. Higher unit cost, predictable billing.
   - Option B (Hybrid Reserved + Burst): Medium reserved pool sized for steady-state; automatic burst into our shared pool for batch windows; supports autoscaling windows and a conservative fallback policy. Lower committed spend, predictable overage cap.

2) Model fallback / fallthrough: yes — Redwood can be configured with automatic fallback rules: route X% of traffic to a quantized 13B variant or a 7B cheaper variant when observed p95 crosses threshold for > 3 consecutive 1-minute windows. We can tie rollback to quality checks and a canary set of prompt tests.

3) Compliance / residency: SOC 2 Type II attached. Data residency: we can provision the reserved pool in US-West-2; we also support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM.

Proposed immediate plan:
- Deliver full price sheet and MAM by EOD Mon Jul 13 (we’ll include legal playbook and DPA redlines).
- Schedule a 90-min tech workshop (Rishi + infra team) for Jul 20–22 (please confirm availability).
- Run a 72-hour canary on a 1-GPU reserved slice if you want to validate p95 under typical traffic.

Next actions (Alex): confirm preferred pricing option and procurement point-of-contact.

Best,
Priya
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

---

Attachment: SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: Dedicated inference reservoir — internal action items

Gentle internal note (do not forward externally): forwarding the thread with asks from CustodyCare. TL;DR and proposed owners: 

- Action: Produce line-item pricing for Option A (strict dedicated) and Option B (hybrid) by EOD Mon Jul 13. Owner: Rishi (pricing + infra sizing).
- Action: Prepare tech workshop agenda with suggested load tests, KV cache warmup strategy, and fallback test plan. Owner: Ben (solutions + ops).
- Action: Draft MAM + procurement checklist including residency & KMS requirements. Owner: Priya (I'll own the MAM & legal touchpoints).
- Note: Alex requested SOC2 and residency (we attached SOC2; verify DPA redlines with legal).

Sizing notes from the call: aim to size for 2k concurrent small requests p50 ~ 80ms baseline, p95 < 350ms; nightly batch window must be handled with burst that completes 6–8M tokens in 2–3 hours. Consider reserve sizing at 4 GPUs or 6 GPUs depending on model quantization path.

I’ll draft the pricing table + MAM and ping legal for DPA redlines — Rishi, flag any infra constraints for US-West provisioning.

Thanks,
Priya
